commitResults.messageBody: Implement deposit (#8) and withdraw (#9). These are the first features that create transactions, so add the shared base they need: Transaction, TransactionList, Command, Parser, Ui and FinNusException. Other commands (balance, recent, delete, help) can be added as new Command subclasses. Parser accepts parameters in any order, rejects invalid amounts (negative, zero, more than 2 decimals, NaN, scientific notation) and requires a description for withdraw. Add JUnit tests for parsing, commands and Transaction formatting.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use BigDecimal for amounts and add no-description deposit constructor
commitResults.messageBody: double cannot represent most decimal values exactly (e.g. 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004), so balances would drift and comparisons could be wrong. BigDecimal keeps amounts exact. Add DepositCommand(BigDecimal) for deposits without a description, as suggested in review. Enable assertions for the Gradle run task.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add deposit and withdraw sections to User Guide
commitResults.messageBody: Document the format, amount rules (positive, at most 2 decimal places, max 1,000,000), optional vs required description, and that parameters can be given in any order. Include examples and expected output so users know what to expect. Replace the template todo example.

The course recommends adding logging to make the code more defensive. Logs go to finnus.log instead of the console, so they never mix with the CLI output the user sees. If the log file cannot be created, logging is turned off instead of stopping the app. Log app start/exit, executed commands, failed commands, parsed input, and added deposits/withdrawals. Ignore log files in git.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add spending categories with t/ and category command
commitResults.messageBody: Implements #61 so users can see where their money goes. Withdrawals take an optional t/CATEGORY (default Others), parsed like c/ via a shared prefix helper instead of a second copy. Categories are checked when the command runs, since custom ones live in TransactionList. category add/list manage custom categories. Categories are saved as CATEGORY records and an extra last TRANSACTION field; rows from older save files load as Others and unknown categories load as Others with a warning, so no spending is lost. UG and DG updated, including withdrawal output examples that now show the category.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search transactions by description
commitResults.messageBody: Users with many transactions had to scroll through recent to find one. find KEYWORD lists matching descriptions, ignoring case, most recent first, numbered with the same index as recent so delete works straight away. Switch the parser test examples from Map.of to Map.ofEntries, which was at its 10-entry limit. UG and DG updated.
Refactored DeveloperGuide.md for neatness and clear sections

commitResults.messageTitle: Record the date of each transaction with on/DATE
commitResults.messageBody: Transactions had no dates, so features like the budget cycle (#60) could not look at spending per period. deposit and withdraw take an optional on/YYYY-MM-DD (default today), parsed with the shared prefix helper; future and non-existent dates are rejected. Today is passed into Parser.parse so tests use a fixed date. The date is shown first on each transaction and saved as an extra last field after the category; field counts stay unambiguous, so older save files load with unknown dates. recent keeps entry order so delete indices never shift. UG and DG updated, including all output examples.

Found in review of #73: LocalDate.parse accepts signed years, so on/-2026-01-01 was accepted and shown as [1 Jan 2027], and on/0001-01-01 also went through. Dates must now match YYYY-MM-DD exactly and be on or after 2000-01-01. The save file loader uses the same rules, so a hand-edited file cannot load such dates either.

Found in review of #71: lowercasing can change the length of some text, e.g. the Turkish capital I with a dot lowercases to two characters, so find istanbul missed Istanbul written with it. Compare one character at a time with regionMatches(true, ...) instead.
